en.name: ApexMarketWatch
en.subtitle: Quotes, charts and 13F filings
en.short_description: Live quotes and charts, plus what the big funds filed with the SEC.
en.description:
ApexMarketWatch is a market watchlist that shows you its sources.

WATCHLIST
Add the tickers you care about and see the last price, the day's high and low, and the 52-week range. Tap through for a price chart and a sparkline over the range you pick.

13F WHALES
Institutional holdings read straight from SEC EDGAR — gross buying, gross selling, and what changed. The SEC's public filing data, not a newsletter's summary of it.

CRASH INDEX
A drawdown-based read on how far a name has fallen from its own high, so a headline number has context.

HONEST PROVENANCE
Every screen labels where its numbers came from. Quotes come from Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint by default; a build can supply a Finnhub key instead. When a source is unavailable the app says so rather than quietly showing you something stale.

NOT ADVICE
ApexMarketWatch reports public market data. It does not recommend trades, hold your money, or connect to a broker.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing ApexMarketWatch.

ApexMarketWatch is a market-data viewer: a watchlist, price charts, 13F institutional filings and a drawdown-based risk score. There is no account, no sign-in, no purchase and no permission request of any kind. It is not a broker: it holds no money, places no orders, connects to no brokerage and makes no recommendation.

Two things worth knowing before you start:
• The app labels the origin of every number. When a feed fails or is not configured, that screen falls back to a bundled offline dataset and shows an amber "sample data" banner naming the reason, plus a provenance footer. Fallback is per feed, not app-wide, so you may legitimately see live quotes next to sample filings. A sample banner is honest labelling, not a crash.
• The Deals tab is sample-only unless the build carries --dart-define=API_GATEWAY_URL. There is no public keyless source for that feed, so by default the tab shows bundled examples above a notice explaining exactly that. Expect it, and please do not treat it as a dead network call.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app. It opens on Markets with a starter watchlist of AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN and TSLA. No sign-in step exists.
2. Pull to refresh. With a network connection, quotes come from Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint, which needs no key; each row shows last price, the day's high and low, and the 52-week range.
3. Tap the + button and add a symbol by ticker or company name (the hint suggests "AAPL, Tesla"). Swipe a row right-to-left to remove it; an undo action appears, and an emptied watchlist stays empty rather than restoring the defaults.
4. Tap a row for the detail screen: a price chart with selectable ranges, range performance, key statistics and any 13F activity in that name.
5. Open the 13F Whales tab. Institutional holdings are read from SEC EDGAR at data.sec.gov, which needs no key but does require a declared contact User-Agent; the app sends "ApexMarketWatch/1.0 (support@americangroupllc.com)". EDGAR rate-limits aggressively, so a refresh may fall back to the bundled dataset with the reason shown.
6. Open Deals — sample-only by default, as described above — then Crash Index, which spells out its own inputs and weights on screen rather than presenting a bare number.
7. Tap the "Data sources" icon in the Markets title bar. It lists each provider (Yahoo Finance, Finnhub, SEC EDGAR, AGL deals gateway) and whether this build has it configured.
8. Turn on airplane mode and pull to refresh. Every tab degrades to the bundled dataset with a banner, and nothing hangs or crashes.

Privacy:
• Data collected: Nothing about you. There is no account and no profile. The watchlist and the chart range are written to shared_preferences on the device.
• Network: Outbound reads only, to Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint and to data.sec.gov. Both are anonymous, and nothing about you is sent beyond the ticker being requested. Finnhub is used only if a build supplies a key.
• Location, camera, contacts, notifications: None are requested; the app has no plugin for any of them.
• Tracking: None. Crash reporting is Firebase Crashlytics only; there is no advertising or analytics SDK, and the app does not read the advertising identifier, so no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
